name: Split Button
hint: Use the caret, then the arrow keys.
description: The main action plus a caret that opens related actions in a menu that grows from the button's edge (and flips above it when there is no room below). Full keyboard menu: arrows, Home/End, a letter jumps, Escape returns focus to the caret, outside press closes. `fullWidth` fills a grid cell or a phone dock.
intents: button with a dropdown of more options
snooze with a choice of times
usage: Use when one action is the obvious default but close variants exist (publish / schedule / draft, snooze / snooze until). If the options are equally likely, use Dropdown Menu instead. Start with `label`, `onClick(event)` for the main half, and `items` (Dropdown Menu's plain objects: {id, label, icon, hint, disabled, danger}, with {separator:true} and {type:'label', label}) with `onSelect(id, item, index)`. With no items it is a plain button with no caret. `fullWidth` makes it fill its container (the main half takes the spare width, the caret keeps its size), so it sits beside a Button in a two-column grid at the same height with no CSS. `loading` is yours to set and clear: it shows a spinner in place, keeps the width and blocks both halves. Control the menu with `open` / `onOpenChange`. The ref and attributes such as `aria-keyshortcuts`, `name`, `value`, `form` and `data-*` go to the main <button>; `className` and `style` go to the root.

dataProps.description: Text of the main half. Blank shows the neutral "Continue" (or the sample "Publish" with `demo`). Also the start of the menu's accessible name ("<label> options").
(event) => void when the main half is pressed. Not called while `loading` or `disabled`; two clicks in the same tick call it once.

The caret's menu, as Dropdown Menu takes it: [{ id, label, icon (icon name or node), hint (or shortcut: short text at the row's end, hidden on touch), disabled, danger, onSelect }], plus { separator: true } and { type: 'label', label } for a group heading. No submenus or checkbox rows. Empty by default; with no items the caret is not rendered and the component is a plain button.

(id, item, index) => void when a menu row is chosen; id falls back to the label, index is the row's position in your `items` array. The menu then closes and focus returns to the caret. Same first two arguments as Dropdown Menu.
Leading icon in the main half: an icon name (sized to `size`) or your own node.
Emphasis, as on Button. Both halves share it.
Height 34 / 42 / 52px, the same as Button's sizes, so the two line up. Both halves grow to at least 44px on touch screens.
The root fills its container's width: the main half takes the spare width and the caret keeps its size. Use it in a grid cell or a phone dock; no CSS needed.
Which edge of the button the menu lines up with. Use "end" when the button sits at the right of its row or screen.
Where the menu opens. "auto" opens below, or above when there is not room below and there is more above (a bottom dock on a phone).

You own it: set it when the action's async work starts and clear it when it ends. The label is replaced by a spinner in place (the width does not change), the main half does not fire or submit, the caret does not open, and an open menu closes.
Native disabled on both halves: not focusable, not clickable, dimmed.
Native type of the main half. Use "submit" inside a <form>; the caret is always type="button" and never submits.
Accessible name of the caret (and of the menu when there is no label), for screen readers.
Controlled open state of the menu. Opening it this way does not move focus; opening from the caret focuses the first row.
Open on mount when uncontrolled.
(open: boolean, reason) => void; reason is "trigger" (the caret), "select", "escape" (Escape or Tab) or "outside".
Fills in the gallery's sample label and items. Your own `label` and `items` win. Off by default; leave it off in real UI.
Added to the root (the element that holds both halves).
Inline style on the root.
Any other attribute (aria-label, aria-describedby, aria-keyshortcuts, id, name, value, form, data-*, tabIndex) goes to the main <button>, as on Button.
Forwarded to the main <button>, so it can be focused (after an error, from a shortcut) or measured.

Where the menu renders. true: through a portal into document.body, carrying the theme tokens found at the button, so an ancestor with overflow:hidden (a card, a table cell), transform or filter can't clip or move it; it follows the button, flips above it and caps its height when squeezed. false: in the button's own DOM (still placed against the viewport). An element or ref: portaled into that element instead.
